results.title: Revolutionizing the lab with AI in laboratory workflows
results.content: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning are no longer just buzzwords — they’re transformative technologies actively reshaping how laboratories operate.1,2 From streamlining workflows to improving real-time decision-making, the use of AI in the laboratory is rapidly becoming an integral component of the modern lab ecosystem.1,2. Machine learning models can synthesize vast amounts of lab data to reveal hidden trends, enabling lab personnel to better anticipate testing needs based on patient volumes and ordering patterns.1,2 They also support operational planning by predicting periods of high demand, helping labs optimize staffing and allocate resources more effectively.6 In fact, clinical laboratories already applying these techniques have reported up to a 30% improvement in staff efficiency.7. Major technology providers are responding with sophisticated, often industry-specific, cloud platforms and AI services designed to manage complex health data, streamline workflows, and enable advanced analytics while navigating stringent security and compliance requirements. results.title: Medical Laboratories in Healthcare Delivery: A Systematic Review ...
results.content: Medical laboratories (MLs) are vital in global healthcare delivery, enhancing diagnostic accuracy and supporting clinical decision-making. These issues include a lack of comprehensive understanding of the roles of medical laboratories (MLs), inconsistent measurement of their impact, integration challenges with other healthcare services, inefficiencies in resource allocation, the rapid pace of technological advancements, and workforce challenges. The integration of molecular testing, the importance of point-of-care diagnostics, the establishment of quality assurance programs, initiatives to build the capacity of laboratory personnel, funding strategies, and infrastructure enhancements were key recommendations for healthcare service improvement [7,8,18,26]. Strengthening the positioning and rationale for the cost-effective QMS model in MLS is essential for enhancing the quality of laboratory services, supporting public health initiatives, and improving patient outcomes. This discussion emphasizes the importance of a cost-effective Quality Management System (QMS) in medical laboratory science (MLS), particularly in LMICs. A robust QMS ensures laboratory test results’ accuracy, reliability, and timeliness, which is critical for effective patient care and clinical decision-making.
